history.period: claimed 302 CE (conflicting sources; one says 12th century)
history.summary: A major Shiva shrine in the Ujjanak area of Kashipur, about 3 km from the bus station, on the banks of the Kosi. The temple's name comes from 'Mota' (large): the Shiva lingam is said to be too large to embrace with two hands and to keep growing. Local tradition calls this the Bheem Shankar Jyotirlingam, the Kama-roop (face) of Shiva, and counts it among the 12 Jyotirlingas - a disputed claim, since the widely recognised Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga is in Maharashtra; treat as a local claim. Mythology ties the site to the ancient Dakini State, the Mahabharata, and a place called Kila where Dronacharya is said to have taught the Kauravas and Pandavas. Sources conflict on age: temple websites claim 302 AD, while another says the structure is 12th century (verify). The complex also has a Bhairav Nath shrine, Shiv Ganga Kund and a Bhagwati Bal-Sundari shrine. CSV town corrected from 'Udham Singh Nagar' to Kashipur.

name: Moteshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Kashipur is a historic city in the Terai region of Udham Singh Nagar district, with roots reaching back to the Vedic-age city of Ujjaini and the 7th-century Govishan visited by Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang. Now a major industrial and educational city and the gateway to Kumaon, it hosts ancient temples, the Drona Sagar lake associated with Guru Dronacharya, and the famous annual Chaiti Mela.

travel.railway: Kashipur Junction Railway Station, about 3 km; linked to Delhi, Lucknow, Moradabad and Varanasi
travel.road: Near the Kashipur bus station (Arya Nagar/Ujjanak area); Kashipur is well connected by road to Delhi and other North Indian cities

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri and the Shravan month are the most festive
